directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Birkin philodendron is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor plant. A spontaneous mutation of the hybrid 'Rojo Congo,' this compact, non-climbing philodendron produces glossy, dark green leaves finely pinstriped with creamy white to pale yellow veins that grow more pronounced as each leaf matures, giving the plant a crisp, sharply patterned look distinct from other variegated philodendrons. Its neat, upright, self-heading rosette habit and modest size make it well suited to a tabletop or shelf as much as a floor specimen, needing no staking or climbing support. Allow the potting mix to dry slightly between waterings and avoid direct sun, which fades the variegation and can scorch the leaves.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Pink Princess philodendron needs strong indirect light to develop and hold its pink variegation and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Pink Princess philodendron needs strong indirect light to develop and hold its pink variegation and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11. This highly sought-after cultivar produces near-black, glossy leaves irregularly splashed and marbled with bright bubblegum-pink patches, a chimeric variegation pattern that varies from leaf to leaf and can revert to solid dark green on stems that receive too little light. Left unstaked it sprawls and vines, but is often grown on a moss pole to encourage larger, more dramatically variegated leaves as the plant matures. Prune out any all-green reverted growth promptly to keep the plant's energy directed toward pink-variegated stems, and rotate the pot regularly for even light exposure.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; White Knight philodendron is frost-tender, slow-growing, and best given a moss pole to climb as it matures.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; White Knight philodendron is frost-tender, slow-growing, and best given a moss pole to climb as it matures. Broad, dark green to near-black leaves marked with irregular patches and speckles of white variegation are carried on thick, dusty-purple to burgundy petioles and stems, a combination of leaf and stem coloring that distinguishes it from the similar but green-stemmed 'White Princess.' As a climbing aroid it develops larger, more heavily variegated foliage when grown vertically on a moss pole or trellis rather than left to trail, and it is prized by collectors for its slow but striking maturation from juvenile to adult leaf form. Keep humidity high, provide strong indirect light to sustain the white variegation, and remove any fully white (chlorophyll-free) growth that cannot photosynthesize and will eventually decline.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Pink Allusion syngonium colors most vividly with bright indirect light and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Pink Allusion syngonium colors most vividly with bright indirect light and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11. Arrow-shaped juvenile leaves emerge a warm coral-pink and mature to a soft rosy-salmon with green margins, a color progression that gives each stem a two-toned, blushing effect distinct from the plain green or white-variegated arrowhead plants more commonly sold. Young plants hold an upright, bushy form and can later be encouraged to climb a moss pole, where mature leaves develop the deeper lobes and arrow shapes typical of adult syngonium foliage. Pinch growing tips to keep the plant compact and bushy, and note that, like other syngoniums, its sap can irritate skin and is toxic if chewed by pets.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; N'Joy pothos is one of the easier variegated pothos selections, tolerating average indoor light and occasional missed waterings.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; N'Joy pothos is one of the easier variegated pothos selections, tolerating average indoor light and occasional missed waterings. Small, compact, heart-shaped leaves are boldly patterned in crisp white and green blocks rather than the finer marbled variegation of marble queen or golden pothos, giving the plant a distinctly patchwork, high-contrast look on a naturally more compact, slower-growing vine. Trailing stems work well in a hanging basket, on a shelf, or trained up a small support, and the plant's smaller stature compared to other pothos cultivars suits tighter spaces such as a desktop or narrow windowsill. Let the potting mix dry between waterings, provide bright indirect light to maintain the crisp variegation, and trim leggy stems to encourage fuller, bushier growth.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, fertile potting mix; Camille dumb cane is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor foliage plant.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, fertile potting mix; Camille dumb cane is frost-tender and grown outdoors only in zones 10-11, elsewhere as an indoor foliage plant. One of the most popular dieffenbachia cultivars, it carries broad, glossy leaves with a bright creamy-yellow to chartreuse center bordered by a distinct dark green margin, brightening low-light corners of a home or shaded patio with strong color contrast. Like all dieffenbachias its thick, cane-like stem and sap contain calcium oxalate crystals that cause intense mouth and throat irritation if chewed, giving rise to the common name 'dumb cane,' so keep it away from curious pets and small children. Water when the top inch of soil dries, wipe dust from the broad leaves periodically to keep pores clear, and cut back leggy canes in spring to encourage bushier new growth from the base.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in moist, well-drained potting mix; Fascinator prayer plant wants high humidity and consistent moisture and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in moist, well-drained potting mix; Fascinator prayer plant wants high humidity and consistent moisture and is frost-tender outside zones 10-11. Oval leaves are patterned with bold reddish-pink veins radiating from the midrib over a rich green background, a striking color combination that intensifies with bright indirect light, and like all prayer plants the leaves fold upward at night and unfurl again each morning in a distinctive daily rhythm. Native to the humid forest floor of Brazil, it thrives in the higher humidity of a bathroom, kitchen, or terrarium-adjacent setting and struggles in dry indoor air, often developing crispy leaf edges without a humidifier or regular misting. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, avoid tap water high in fluoride or chlorine if leaf tips brown, and divide congested clumps in spring to propagate and renew vigor.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference
